articles.title: Israel elections 2026: What's at stake for Netanyahu? Key challengers, seats needed to win and more
articles.summary: Israel is set to vote on Tuesday, marking its first national election since Hamas’ October 7, 2023, attack, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s
articles.body: Israel is set to vote on Tuesday, marking its first national election since Hamas’ October 7, 2023, attack, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s leadership, security record and political future at the centre of the campaign.Voters are weighing his handling of the attack and the conflicts that followed against concerns over military service exemptions, judicial reforms and the rising cost of living.With Netanyahu facing a challenge from rival parties, the election is expected to test his ability to retain power after years of conflict and political divisions.However, with no single party expected to win a majority in the 120-member Knesset, the next government will depend on post-election coalition negotiations as much as the vote itself.What will decide Israel’s electionIsrael’s first national election since Hamas’ October 7, 2023, attack is widely seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s leadership. While the attack and the security failures surrounding it remain central to the campaign, the debate has focused largely on Netanyahu’s accountability, his handling of the aftermath and his leadership rather than Israel’s military conduct in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, which has broad domestic support.One of the biggest issues is the exemption of ultra-Orthodox Jewish men from compulsory military service. With Israel facing a shortage of soldiers and reservists repeatedly called up during wars, the exemptions have fuelled resentment among secular Israelis. Netanyahu’s dependence on ultra-Orthodox parties has made the issue particularly contentious, with his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, promising to end the exemptions.Netanyahu’s proposed judicial overhaul, which triggered mass protests in 2023, remains another point of division. Critics see the changes as an attempt to weaken the Supreme Court and undermine democratic institutions, while Netanyahu has defended them as a way to curb judicial power. The economy and the rising cost of living are also concerns, although they have received relatively little attention during the campaign despite many Israelis struggling with affordability.Leadership is likely to be a decisive factor, with voters weighing Netanyahu’s experience and security record against criticism of his handling of October 7 and the wars that followed.However, neither of the main political blocs is advocating a major shift on the Palestinian question: both are dominated by parties that support Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank and oppose the establishment of a Palestinian state. With no party expected to win an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset, the outcome will also depend on which leader can assemble a governing coalition.Who are the leading candidates?Benjamin Netanyahu: Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, Netanyahu has been in power for much of the period since 2009. His supporters see him as a strong leader capable of defending Israel, but his political standing has been weakened by the security failures surrounding Hamas’ October 7, 2023, attack, his corruption trial and an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over alleged war crimes in Gaza, which he denies. His Likud party has faced a decline in opinion polls, though Netanyahu remains a formidable political survivor and is seeking to form a broad national government.Gadi Eisenkot: The former military chief, 66, leads the centrist Yashar party and has positioned himself as a security-focused alternative to Netanyahu. Having lost his son in combat in Gaza, Eisenkot has highlighted his military background and personal sacrifices. He has also pledged to end the exemptions from compulsory military service enjoyed by ultra-Orthodox men, an issue that has become a major source of public anger.Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid: Former prime ministers Bennett, 54, and Lapid have joined forces under a new party called Together. Bennett is a former commando and a right-wing politician, while Lapid comes from the centre. Despite their different political backgrounds, the two previously worked together to oust Netanyahu in 2021. Their campaign has focused on national unity and getting Israel back on track after years of conflict and political division.Avigdor Lieberman: The former defence minister, 68, leads the right-wing Israel Our Home party, which draws considerable support from Israel’s ex-Soviet immigrant community. Once a close ally of Netanyahu, Lieberman left his government in 2018, accusing him of being too soft on Palestinian militants in Gaza. He has since become one of the prime minister’s most vocal critics.Yair Golan: The former general, 64, heads the Democrats, a left-wing party formed from the remnants of Israel’s Labour party and Meretz. Golan was praised for helping rescue people from a site targeted during the October 7 attack.Key figures backing NetanyahuFinance minister Bezalel Smotrich, 46, and national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, 50, are prominent far-right allies of Netanyahu. Smotrich has pushed for expanding Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank and opposed Palestinian statehood. Ben-Gvir has advocated tougher measures against Palestinian prisoners, capital punishment for convicted Palestinian militants and expanded gun ownership for Israelis. Both have also backed the expulsion of Palestinians from Gaza and Israeli resettlement of the enclave.Netanyahu has also depended on the ultra-Orthodox parties Shas and United Torah Judaism to maintain his governing coalitions. Their demand to preserve exemptions from compulsory military service for many ultra-Orthodox men has become increasingly contentious as Israel faces wartime manpower shortages.Who could hold the balance of power?Parties that are not firmly aligned with either major bloc could prove decisive in determining who forms the next government. These include Raam and the Joint List, which represent Israel’s Arab minority, as well as the new right-wingPeople of Israel party and the centre-right Reservists party. Their final strength and willingness to join either camp could shape coalition negotiations after the vote.How elections work in IsraelIsrael follows a proportional representation system to elect the 120 members of its parliament, the Knesset. Voters choose political parties rather than individual candidates, and seats are distributed according to each party’s share of the national vote. Parties must secure at least 3.25% of the vote to enter parliament.Since no single party has ever won an outright majority, forming a government typically requires alliances between multiple parties. The leader who can assemble a coalition with the support of at least 61 lawmakers can form the government, giving smaller parties considerable influence over negotiations and policy decisions.The election comes after a period of political instability between 2019 and 2022, when Israel held repeated elections. Netanyahu’s current Knesset is among the few in the country’s history to have completed its full four-year term.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban said that he is “not a doomer” regarding the rise of artificial intelligence (AI), arguing that organisations can
articles.body: Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban said that he is “not a doomer” regarding the rise of artificial intelligence (AI), arguing that organisations can effectively protect themselves from AI-powered cyberattacks by deploying the very same technology on defense. Speaking at the Reuters Total Health conference, the former Shark Tank investor compared malicious AI agents to household pests, introducing what he called his "Cockroach Theory" of cybersecurity.“I’m not a doomer at all. We hear about the worst possible scenarios with AI, but we don’t talk about the defensive measures that that same capable AI can take against them,” Cuban said.The investor added: “It’s like the cockroach thing, right? You build a new house, you get the guys to come out and spray... the one thing I don’t want is cockroaches in my house ever. But the cockroaches find a way to get in because there’s zillions of them, right? And then if there’s one gets in, there’s more that are going to get in, and that’s kind of the way AI works.”Cuban explained that if bad actors build swarms of autonomous agents to probe networks through sheer numbers, defenders can respond with equal computational power.“It’s like the Cockroach theory, where if somebody can create enough agents, it’ll find a way to get in, and then it just exploits that. But the good news is, you can spray your systems with just as much AI,” he said, adding, “It's all brute force acts, and if it's brute force on that side with the bad guys, you can also use brute force with the good guys... And I think there’s going to be more effort from the good guys trying to stop the bad guys.”Expanding cost plus drugs into portable manufacturingBeyond his perspective on emerging technology, Cuban discussed the rapid evolution of his healthcare enterprise, Cost Plus Drug Company. Launched in 2022 to disrupt traditional pharmaceutical pricing, Cost Plus operates on a transparent model: charging the wholesale cost it pays for a medication plus a fixed 15% markup. In May, the business joined TrumpRx.gov, a platform established by the Trump administration to distribute discounted weight-loss medications.The venture has since broadened its footprint from retail distribution to direct manufacturing. In 2025, Cost Plus began producing sterile injectable medications commonly required by hospitals at its own dedicated compounding facility.Cuban revealed that the company has now engineered compact, tractor-trailer-sized manufacturing units that he terms “pods.” Designed to function independently or link together, these mobile units can manufacture generic medications as well as specialized treatments for rare diseases.You use AI every day. articles.title: Can the man Trump called a 'jihadist' become America's first Muslim senator?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With just over a week left for the US midterm elections, a Senate race in Michigan has drawn national attention.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With just over a week left for the US midterm elections, a Senate race in Michigan has drawn national attention. US President Donald Trump unleashed a series of attacks on Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, calling him a "jihadist" and accusing him of having links to extremist groups. El-Sayed is seeking to become America's first Muslim senator in the November 3 midterm elections.At a campaign rally in Port Huron, Trump called El-Sayed a "jihadist" who was "on the side of the terrorists" and claimed he would "have to go through a metal detector before he's allowed to go into the Senate."Trump also referred to the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, comparing efforts to stop El-Sayed from entering the Senate with the passengers who fought back against hijackers aboard United Airlines Flight 93.The president accused El-Sayed of having links to the Muslim Brotherhood and wanting to impose sharia law. However, no evidence has been presented linking El-Sayed to the organisation, and he has repeatedly denied the allegations.Who is Abdul El-Sayed?Born in the United States to Egyptian immigrant parents, El-Sayed is a physician and epidemiologist who previously served as Detroit's health director.He unsuccessfully contested Michigan's Democratic gubernatorial primary in 2018 before winning the party's Senate nomination in August 2026.His campaign focuses on healthcare, affordable housing and economic inequality. He has also criticised US military assistance to Israel.What has El-Sayed said?Responding to Trump at a rally in Grand Rapids on Sunday, El-Sayed accused the president of using his name and religion to distract voters from economic concerns."They think that by pointing at my name and my faith, that somehow you're going to ignore the fact that you can't afford your gas or your groceries, can't see a doctor," he said.El-Sayed also responded to Trump's repeated use of his middle name."I don't even care that he remembers my whole name because he can just go on and call me 'senator' after November," he said. "I will be Senator Muhammad to you, bro."His Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, has also questioned his loyalty to the United States."Are you for America, or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?" Rogers asked during a debate.El-Sayed called the question "shameful", adding: "I'm proud of our Constitution that guarantees all of us the right to pray as we choose to pray."Trump's remarks also drew criticism from Bishara Bahbah, a founder of Arab Americans for Trump, a group that supported the president's outreach to Arab American voters in 2024."The president's statements are out of line," Bahbah said. "They are crossing a red line. They are racist."Can El-Sayed win the Michigan Senate race?El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers, a former congressman, in the November 3 election for the seat being vacated by Democratic Senator Gary Peters.The contest is closely fought. According to the RealClearPolling average of surveys conducted between September 24 and October 22, El-Sayed was ahead of Rogers by 47.9% to 46%, a difference of 1.9 percentage points.Former President Barack Obama campaigned for El-Sayed in Michigan on Saturday, while Senator Bernie Sanders has also backed his candidacy.Michigan is an important state in the battle for control of the US Senate. Republicans have not won a Senate election in the state for more than three decades.The state also has a large Arab American population, particularly in Dearborn, which Trump won in 2024 amid dissatisfaction with the Biden administration's handling of the Gaza war.If El-Sayed wins on November 3, he will become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Israel's defence minister Israel Katz on Monday denied reports of a rift between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Israel Defence Forces (IDF) Chief
articles.body: Israel's defence minister Israel Katz on Monday denied reports of a rift between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Israel Defence Forces (IDF) Chief of Staff Lt General Eyal Zamir over possible military action against Iran, calling the allegations “completely baseless and false” and saying Israel had no intention of launching an attack before Tuesday's elections.According to The Times of Israel, the denial followed reports by Israeli broadcaster Channel 12 that Netanyahu and Zamir were at odds over an unspecified military operation linked to Iran, which security officials reportedly feared could trigger a wider confrontation on the eve of the election. Army Radio reported similar details on Monday, citing two senior security officials.“The reports of disagreements between the political leadership and the IDF on Iran are completely baseless and false,” Katz said in a statement.“I state unequivocally that Israel had no intention of initiating an attack on Iran before the elections in Israel, while making clear that if Iran attacks Israel, we will respond with great force,” he added.Netanyahu also dismissed the allegations as “nonsense” in an interview with Israel's Channel 14, according to The Times of Israel. However, in an earlier television appearance, the Israeli prime minister said he had instructed the IDF and Mossad to work towards toppling the Iranian regime.The controversy follows a report by Channel 12 on Sunday night that Zamir had resisted carrying out an unspecified military action allegedly instructed by Netanyahu. According to the broadcaster, Zamir sought further deliberations and signed documentation from the prime minister regarding legal authorisation for the operation.The report did not disclose the nature of the proposed action or its intended targets, although it linked the alleged instructions to a possible fresh strike on Iran. Channel 12 quoted an unnamed military source as saying, “This relates to an action that could lead to a flare-up with Iran, at a sensitive and dramatic moment, creating this potential miscalculation.”The broadcaster also cited unnamed sources who expressed concern that the political leadership could seek to use the Iran issue for political benefit.Israel polls on knife edge as Netanyahu faces backlash over Iran rowOpinion polls published ahead of Tuesday's parliamentary elections show a tight contest, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition assured of a majority in the 120-member Knesset.The final surveys by Israel's public broadcaster KAN and Channel 12 projected 52 seats for the opposition camp led by Gadi Eisenkot, against 50 for Netanyahu's bloc, leaving both short of the 61 seats needed to form a government.Opposition leaders have accused Netanyahu of putting political survival ahead of national security by allegedly pushing for military action against Iran on the eve of the election.Avigdor Liberman has sought a criminal investigation into Netanyahu over alleged treason, while Eisenkot warned that the military must not be used as a tool in the prime minister's political campaign.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1974, just four Mauritius kestrels remained in the wild; then Carl Jones brought the bird back from the brink of extinction, with numbers reaching around 600
articles.summary: The Mauritius kestrel was once so close to extinction that only four known individuals remained in the wild, including a single breeding pair.
articles.body: The Mauritius kestrel was once so close to extinction that only four known individuals remained in the wild, including a single breeding pair. Its survival seemed increasingly uncertain until Welsh conservationist Carl Jones and a team of researchers began an intensive effort to save the species. Through captive breeding, careful monitoring, supplementary feeding and the protection of nesting sites, conservationists gradually rebuilt its population. Their efforts helped the bird recover to around 600 individuals at its historical peak, making it one of the most remarkable examples of wildlife conservation. However, the comeback did not mark the end of the story. The Mauritius kestrel remains endangered, and continuing threats to its habitat show how difficult it can be to sustain a conservation success over the long term.How the Mauritius kestrel reached the brink of extinctionThe Mauritius kestrel (Falco punctatus) is a bird of prey found naturally only on the island of Mauritius in the Indian Ocean. Its population collapsed over several decades as human activity transformed the island's natural environment.Extensive forest destruction deprived the birds of their habitat, while the widespread use of pesticides further contributed to their decline. By the 1950s, the kestrel had become restricted to the Black River Gorges region. In 1974, only four individuals were known to survive in the wild, including a single breeding pair, making the species one of the most endangered birds in the world.The conservationist who refused to give upCarl Jones, a Welsh conservation biologist, became a central figure in the effort to save the Mauritius kestrel. His work in Mauritius formed part of a wider conservation career focused on rescuing endangered species.According to the Mauritian Wildlife Foundation, Jones arrived on the island when many people believed the kestrel's recovery was unlikely. Some feared that the tiny population would not survive, while others questioned whether conservation resources should be spent on a species with such uncertain prospects.Jones continued working on the recovery effort, helping develop methods to increase breeding success and improve the birds' chances of survival. He later became chief scientist at the Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust and scientific director of the Mauritian Wildlife Foundation. His conservation work also contributed to recovery efforts involving other endangered Mauritian birds.How conservationists brought the kestrel backSaving the Mauritius kestrel required more than protecting the few birds that remained. Conservationists needed to increase breeding success, raise young birds and establish populations in suitable habitats.The recovery programme combined several techniques, including captive breeding, the release of birds into the wild, supplementary feeding and the provision of artificial nesting sites. Researchers also monitored breeding pairs and worked to reduce threats around nests.One important technique involved manipulating the birds' breeding cycles. Conservationists could remove eggs for incubation, encouraging females to lay another clutch. This approach helped increase the number of young birds produced, while artificial nest sites and predator management improved the chances of successful breeding.The programme was a long-term effort involving Jones and other researchers, local conservationists, government agencies and international organisations. Its success depended on combining scientific research with intensive, practical management of the birds and their habitats.From four wild birds to hundredsThe recovery was gradual rather than immediate. By the end of the intensive restoration programme in 1994, the post-breeding population was estimated at between 222 and 286 birds. By 2000, estimates had risen to between 500 and 800 individuals.The Mauritian Wildlife Foundation describes the population's rise from four known wild birds in 1974 to a peak of around 600 as one of the most successful species recovery programmes. The differing figures reflect estimates made at different points in the recovery, rather than a single fixed population count.The comeback also helped establish the Mauritius kestrel as an important example of what sustained conservation intervention can achieve. A bird once considered close to extinction had returned to several parts of the island through captive breeding, reintroductions and continued monitoring.Why the Mauritius kestrel is struggling againThe historic recovery did not eliminate the threats facing the species. Habitat degradation, introduced predators and competition continue to affect Mauritius kestrels, while the island has lost much of its original forest.The Mauritian Wildlife Foundation has documented contrasting trends across different parts of the island. The population in the Bambous Mountains in the east grew from about 40 pairs to approximately 50 breeding pairs and remained relatively stable for a period. In contrast, the population in and around the Black River Gorges declined from an estimated 40 to 50 pairs in the mid-1990s to about 20 pairs in 2021.The International Union for Conservation of Nature's 2023 assessment lists the Mauritius kestrel as Endangered, with a decreasing population trend. It identifies continuing habitat decline and the effects of introduced species among the pressures facing the bird. The assessment also estimated 140 to 170 mature individuals, a measure that should not be confused with the total number of birds of all ages.Conservation work continuesEfforts to protect the Mauritius kestrel continue through monitoring, breeding management and research. In March 2025, the Mauritian Wildlife Foundation reported that its fauna team had been ringing and measuring kestrel chicks and collecting blood samples. The work helps researchers identify individual birds, gather biological information and determine which conservation measures may be needed to support the population.You use AI every day. articles.title: Fake papers & trade contracts: How Myanmar dodged US sanctions to get Iranian jet fuel - report
articles.summary: Myanmar allegedly disguised Iranian jet fuel as South African diesel to bypass US sanctions, using trade contracts and import documents that
articles.body: Myanmar allegedly disguised Iranian jet fuel as South African diesel to bypass US sanctions, using trade contracts and import documents that misrepresented the cargo's origin and nature, a Reuters investigation has found.According to Reuters report, a December 2025 shipment of around 113,000 barrels of Iranian jet fuel was covered by a $15.8 million contract between Myanmar-based Dynamic Wave and Thailand's Tawan-Oil Trading that described the cargo as South African diesel. Myanmar's foreign exchange regulator also authorised documents identifying the shipment as diesel rather than jet fuel, the investigation found.The alleged deception comes as Washington seeks to restrict fuel supplies that could help Myanmar's military sustain airstrikes against civilians. The trade also exposes the challenges of enforcing US sanctions on Iran when shipments pass through regional intermediaries and are accompanied by documents that obscure their origin.The findings are particularly significant as the United States has recently reopened limited diplomatic contacts with Myanmar's military-backed government, raising questions about how Washington will balance engagement with continued pressure over the military's conduct and its access to restricted supplies.The December shipment was not an isolated case. Reuters found that an earlier transaction in May 2025 involved a contract for 202,000 barrels of fuel worth $26 million, also described as South African diesel. The tanker Noble subsequently arrived in Yangon carrying just under 200,000 barrels of jet fuel, with satellite analysis tracing the shipment to Iran.The shipments highlight the restrictions facing Myanmar's military-linked aviation sector. In August 2023, the US Treasury announced sanctions targeting foreign individuals and entities operating in Myanmar's jet-fuel sector, seeking to disrupt supplies that Washington said enabled the military to carry out airstrikes against civilians.Iranian fuel presents an additional sanctions risk because Washington maintains separate measures targeting Iran's petroleum trade. By describing the cargo as South African diesel, the companies involved in the reported transactions obscured two critical details: the fuel's actual origin and its identity as aviation fuel.You use AI every day. articles.title: Shut since 1943, this hidden Natural History Museum gallery in London is open again with a 400,000-year-old handaxe and a 1980s Star Wars toy encrusted with marine life
articles.summary: Natural History Museum London hidden gallery reopening: a second-floor space in the Waterhouse building, shut to the public since 1943, has welcomed
articles.body: Natural History Museum London hidden gallery reopening: a second-floor space in the Waterhouse building, shut to the public since 1943, has welcomed visitors again after more than 80 years. Its opening exhibition, Nature and Us, gathers 50 objects that show how people have imagined, exploited and reinterpreted the natural world, including a handaxe made 400,000 years ago. Admission is free, and the exhibition will run for an initial 18 months. Behind the exhibition stands a collection of more than 80 million specimens spanning 4.5 billion years, which the museum calls the most important of its kind anywhere in the world.Why the beautiful Waterhouse building gallery vanished from public view during the Second World WarBefore it closed, the room worked as two galleries in one: an osteology gallery devoted to skeletons, and a mammals gallery. Historic photographs released by the Natural History Museum show it as the Osteology gallery in 1893 and as the Upper Mammals Gallery in 1911.Everything changed when the museum’s original herbarium, its collection of preserved plants, was damaged during the Second World War. The room was repurposed to house the botanical collections and was no longer open to visitors. Its original wooden herbarium cabinets remain in place, a reminder of its long life as a working space for scientific collections.From a 400,000-year-old handaxe to a Star Wars toy: the objects telling nature’s storyThe exhibition moves well beyond fossils and skeletons. A miniature model of a Crystal Palace dinosaur shows how early scientists and artists pictured prehistoric life. Jenny, a Victorian skeleton of a monk seal, reveals how wild animals were once exploited for entertainment.Some objects are far more ordinary. A toy from the Star Wars films, made in the 1980s and now encrusted with bryozoans (tiny water-dwelling animals), shows how everyday items can take on new meanings through contact with nature and the passing of time. The handaxe, meanwhile, is an object whose discovery transformed understanding of when humans first existed.Visitors can also touch a replica jaw from one of Britain’s earliest known domesticated dogs, which lived around 14,300 years ago and offers evidence of the long bond between people and dogs.A visitor-led experiment that will shape the permanent gallery planned to open in 2029The content of Nature and Us is deliberately experimental. Visitors can have their say, and their responses will help decide which stories appear in the permanent gallery that is due to open in 2029.Claire Andrews, Head of Community Engagement at the Natural Environment Research Council, said in the museum’s announcement that the space would help audiences explore their connection with nature. She added that she was confident it would captivate minds and encourage people to examine their own relationship with the natural world and how science can drive action for the planet.The wider plan to open a new or refreshed Natural History Museum gallery every year to 2031The reopening is part of the museum’s campaign to transform its South Kensington building ahead of its 150th anniversary in 2031. The plan is to open a brand new or revitalised gallery every year until then, with the aim of welcoming 1 million more visitors annually and engaging 10 million schoolchildren, families and changemakers.It follows the gallery Fixing Our Broken Planet, which the museum says has been visited by 3 million people since opening in 2025. The campaign is also seeking to raise an additional £150 million.Doug Gurr, the museum’s director, said in the announcement that the reopening was “an exciting moment for the Museum” and that new spaces like this are meant to inspire people to become advocates for the planet. The museum’s stated mission is to create more than 100 million of them by 2031.Who funded the reopening and how to visit the gallery on Cromwell Road in South KensingtonNature and Us opened to the public on 16 September. The Natural Environment Research Council, part of UK Research and Innovation, is the lead funder. Björn Savén is the associate funder, and the museum also thanked Ned F. Kuehn, Roger Gahagan, the Edith Murphy Foundation and The James & Shirley Sherwood Foundation for their support.The museum is on Cromwell Road, London SW7 5BD, and is open daily from 10:00 to 17:50. It is closed from 24 to 26 December.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: BJP protests across states over Kharge's 'baap' remark at PM Modi; demands apology
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP workers on Monday staged protests in Bihar, Jammu and Bengaluru against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's controversial 'baap' remark
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP workers on Monday staged protests in Bihar, Jammu and Bengaluru against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's controversial 'baap' remark against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding an apology from the Congress chief.The protests came a day after Kharge, speaking at an event in Patna, responded to a person from the audience who said that PM Modi would not go anywhere. "Modi ka baap bhi jayega (Even Modi's father will have to go)," Kharge said, triggering criticism from BJP leaders.The remark was made during a programme marking the 139th birth anniversary of Bihar's first chief minister, Shrikrishna Singh.Delhi BJP workers hold protest outside Kharge's residenceDelhi BJP workers and leaders staged a protest near Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence on Rajaji Marg on Monday over his alleged disparaging remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The protest turned tense as demonstrators attempted to break through police barricades and march towards Kharge's residence.Police stopped the protesters as they tried to march from Sena Bhawan circle towards the Congress president's residence. Around 2,000 BJP workers and leaders, including Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra, were detained, the Delhi BJP said in a statement.Amid heavy police deployment in the Sena Bhawan area, the detained BJP workers and leaders were packed into buses and taken to Mandir Marg police station. They were later released, according to the party's statement.The BJP had called for nationwide protests over Kharge's remarks at an event in Patna, escalating its confrontation with the Congress over the alleged comments against the prime minister.BJP leaders detained during Bengaluru protestIn Bengaluru, BJP leaders and workers staged a demonstration at Freedom Park, demanding an unconditional apology from Kharge over his remarks.Police detained several BJP leaders, including Karnataka assembly leader of opposition R Ashoka and former minister CN Ashwath Narayan, during the protest.BJP leaders accused the Congress president of making offensive remarks against the Prime Minister and his family.BJP workers burn Kharge's effigy in PatnaIn Patna, BJP workers took out a 'Jan Akrosh March' under the leadership of Bihar BJP president Sanjay Saraogi.The protesters marched from the party headquarters towards Income Tax Golambar, raising slogans against Kharge and the Congress. They also burnt an effigy of the Congress president."Yesterday, all limits were crossed when the platform to celebrate the birth anniversary of Shrikrishna Singh, the architect of modern Bihar, was used to make abusive remarks about the late father of the Prime Minister," Saraogi said.He accused the Congress of making personal attacks against Modi out of political frustration and demanded an apology from Kharge and Rahul Gandhi."The Congress, Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi must apologise to the people of the country," he said.Protests in Jammu, other districtsIn Jammu, BJP leaders and workers staged a protest at Dogra Chowk, raising slogans against Kharge and the Congress. Led by BJP MLA Shagun Parihar and Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha's Jammu and Kashmir president Arun Prabhat, the protesters marched through Dogra Chowk, burnt posters of Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, and staged a brief sit-in on the road.Parihar condemned the remarks, saying they were disrespectful not only to the Prime Minister's late father but also to elderly people who had passed away."If they do not respect the prime minister's father, how will they respect the father of an ordinary citizen?" she asked. Protests were also reported from Samba, Kathua, Poonch, Udhampur, Rajouri, Doda, Kishtwar and Reasi districts. Similar demonstrations were held in Delhi and Lucknow as part of the BJP's nationwide protest against Kharge's remarks.Congress defends Kharge's remarksMeanwhile, the Congress defended its president, claiming that a BJP supporter had first insulted Kharge's father during the Patna event. Congress leader Pawan Khera said Kharge was referring to the RSS as PM Modi's "ideological father", rather than his biological father. RJD leader Bhai Virendra also defended Kharge, describing his remarks as a "slip of the tongue" and saying he did not need to apologise.However, RJD MP Manoj Jha said such conduct was not expected from a senior leader like Kharge, while questioning what he described as selective outrage over remarks made by political leaders. Union home minister Amit Shah also criticised Kharge, accusing the Congress of repeatedly crossing the limits of political decorum by targeting PM Modi and his family.Defence minister Rajnath Singh slammed Congress presidentDefence Minister Rajnath Singh on Monday slammed Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his controversial remark about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s late father, saying the statement had left him shocked and hurt. He also criticised the Congress for defending Kharge’s comments instead of expressing regret over the controversy.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

Earlier in the interview, he said he had recently “instructed the IDF and Mossad to topple the [Iranian] regime”, although it was unclear whether the remark was connected to the reported instruction.The reports came as US President Donald Trump renewed his endorsement of Netanyahu on Sunday, urging Israelis to vote for the prime minister in Tuesday’s election.In a post on Truth Social, Trump praised their relationship and called Netanyahu an “outstanding Warrior Prime Minister”. He also urged voters to back Netanyahu, writing: “Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister, we have to finish the job that we started.”Netanyahu also posted an AI-generated image depicting a nuclear explosion in Tel Aviv on Sunday. articles.title: 'Thank God Ram didn't hit minority': UP CEO on caste bias allegations over voter slips row
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa on Monday responded to allegations of caste bias over an erroneous voter slip, saying that
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa on Monday responded to allegations of caste bias over an erroneous voter slip, saying that computers and software are not casteist.This comes after AAP Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Singh questioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over an erroneous entry in a voter slip where "Ramhit Yadav" became "Ram ne Yadav ko Maara".In a post on X in Hindi, Singh said, "Gyanesh Kumar ji, why did Ram hit only a Yadav? Why did Ram not hit any Singh, Pathak, Asthana, Sharma, Rai or Bisht? Is your computer casteist? Are you running the agenda of any political party?"In a sarcastic reply to Singh, Rinwa said that had the entry read Ram hit a minority (alpasankhyak), the authorities would have been accused of communalism too."A strange name, 'Ram ne Sharma ko Maara', is also present in the voter list of the recent legislative council elections. Computers/software are not casteist," the UP CEO said."We accept that an error was made, but fortunately, even while making the error, no caste discrimination took place. Thank God that Ram did not hit a minority. Otherwise, besides being accused of casteism, we would have also faced allegations of communalism," he added.The CEO's office also shared a voter slip from the recently held graduate constituency legislative council elections. The slip listed the voter's name as Ravi Sharma, while his father's name appeared as "Ram ne Sharma ko Maara".The exchange comes days after instances of erroneous entries in electoral records were flagged, raising questions over the computer software used to prepare voter lists.Later, Rinwa, in a post on X, said some "bizarre-looking names" had appeared in the voter list during the recently held legislative council elections."The reasons behind such mistakes are being looked into and appropriate action is being taken to prevent recurrence," the CEO said.He said "some forged voter slips" had gone viral on social media and were being displayed or circulated by several established media outlets and prominent individuals. "The person responsible for the forgery will be dealt with as per law," Rinwa added.Last week, Rinwa had explained that the software was designed to transliterate names entered in English into Hindi.However, in some cases, instead of transliterating names, it translated the words, resulting in incorrect entries. For instance, if "Ramhit Yadav" was mistakenly typed as "Ram Hit Yadav", the software translated it into Hindi as "Ram ne Yadav ko Maara" (Ram hit Yadav).He said the errors could have been corrected using the editing feature, but some remained in the final list.Another instance, in which "B.Com" was entered in place of the father's name in the electoral roll for the legislative council polls, appeared to be a case of human error or negligence, the CEO had said.Polling for 11 seats in the Uttar Pradesh legislative council was held on October 23, and counting of votes will take place on October 27.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: CHENNAI: The Central Crime Branch (CCB) of the Chennai police on Monday arrested former Tamil Nadu school education minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi in
articles.body: CHENNAI: The Central Crime Branch (CCB) of the Chennai police on Monday arrested former Tamil Nadu school education minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi in connection with an alleged Rs 100crore scam involving the issuance of recognition and other statutory clearances to private schools.A CCB team reached his apartment in Aminjikarai and arrested him after Madras high court dismissed his anticipatory bail application.The case was registered based on a complaint lodged by D C Elangovan, secretary of the Federation of Associations of Private Schools in Tamil Nadu. In his complaint, Elangovan alleged that B T Arasakumar and Muthukumar, who claimed to be the founder-president and treasurer, respectively, of the Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association, an unregistered organisation, had collected more than Rs 100 crore from private school managements.The accused allegedly promised to secure permanent recognition from govt, approvals for upgrading schools, Directorate of Town and Country Planning (DTCP) clearances and other statutory permissions. The money was collected under the guise of contributions towards "party funds" for DMK, which was in power at the time.Arasakumar claimed to have contacts within the govt and assured private school administrators that he could arrange the required permissions. However, he neither fulfilled his promises nor returned the money.The CCB initially registered a case against Arasakumar under Section 7 (acceptance or demand of a bribe) and Section 12 (abetment of offences) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.Arasakumar was arrested by the CCB on June 27. Based on subsequent inquiries, investigators began probing the involvement of Anbil Mahesh, who was the school education minister at the time.On Sept 16, CCB teams conducted searches at nine locations in Chennai and Trichy, including four premises linked to Mahesh, and seized several documents. articles.title: Congress to hold ‘Vote Bachao' rally at Ramlila Maidan on Nov 1; Amit Shah to lead padayatra in T'gana on Nov 2
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Congress will hold a ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ mega rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on November 1, party president Mallikarjun Kharge
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Congress will hold a ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ mega rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on November 1, party president Mallikarjun Kharge said on Monday. The protest comes over the alleged vote theft, demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an immediate halt of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).Meanwhile, Union home minister Amit Shah is also set to attend a BJP foot march in Telangana a day later, on November 2, to counter what the party calls the Congress's “false narrative” against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao announced Shah's participation in the November 2 ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ (save democracy, remove anarchy) padayatra on Monday.The announcement comes amid a political row over the SIR exercise, with the Congress accusing the Election Commission of large-scale electoral irregularities.“They (Congress) are trying to create anarchy in the state and country. That's why we are going to organise a padayatra with the theme 'Loktantra Bachao - Arajakta Hatao' (save democracy - remove anarchy). Amit Shah ji will attend the padayatra on 2nd (of November),” news agency PTI reported, quoting Rao.Kharge announces mega rally at Ramleela MaidanKharge announced the November 1 rally in a video shared on X, alleging that the constitutional right to vote of millions of Indians was under threat.“The constitutional right of the Indian people to cast their votes is under threat. CEC Gyanesh Kumar is solely responsible for this; he has acted entirely at the behest of the Prime Minister and the Home Minister,” Kharge said.Kharge also criticised the government over inflation.In his video address, he said, “Greetings, friends. It is the festive season, yet you are currently grappling with back-breaking inflation. The government, however, is completely unconcerned—all they know how to do is steal votes. Large-scale vote theft has taken place, and it continues even now.”Announcing the rally, he said, “In this regard, a 'Save the Vote, Save the Nation' (Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao) mega-rally will be held on November 1st at the historic Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi.”“I appeal to you to participate actively in this rally to protect our Constitution and democracy, and to help make this campaign a success. Long live the Constitution! Jai Hind!” he added.BJP challenges Congress over SIR claimsRao accused the Congress of spreading misinformation about the electoral roll revision and challenged Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy to identify voters whose names had been wrongly deleted.Observing that Congress was spreading lies over the SIR exercise, Rao said he was ready to visit the chief minister's native village, Kondareddypalle, to check how many voters' names had been removed from the rolls.He said genuine voters whose names were deleted had the option of getting them included again. Rao also asked Congress ministers in Telangana to identify at least 10 voters whose names had been deleted and explain the reasons for their removal.Responding to allegations that 13 crore voters had been removed during the SIR exercise, Rao claimed that they fell into the categories of 'Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate' (ASDD).Of these, he claimed, 2.8 crore were dead, three crore were absent or untraceable when booth-level officers visited them, 6.3 crore had permanently shifted and nearly one crore names were registered at multiple locations. He cited the example of a man in Hyderabad who had admitted to having voter registrations at three places.Rao targets Kharge, Congress over rallyRao also criticised Kharge over his remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging that Congress was unable to accept that a 'chaiwala' had become the country's Prime Minister. He said the party was desperate to return to power after losing elections since 2014.The Telangana BJP president asked party workers to burn Congress effigies at district headquarters on Monday in protest against Kharge's remarks.He also took exception to Congress leaders from Telangana travelling to Delhi for the November 1 rally, citing water shortages in the state. Rao claimed that more than 300 of Telangana's over 600 mandals were facing drought-like conditions due to a rainfall deficit.Pointing to the impact of El Nino on water availability in Hyderabad, he said around 8,000 water tankers were being booked daily in the city. He urged Revanth Reddy to focus on addressing the water crisis instead.On the chief minister's recent pitch for Rahul Gandhi to become Prime Minister, Rao said the BJP's graph had risen since Gandhi began occupying leadership positions in the Congress.Taking a swipe at the Congress leader, Rao said, "you cannot market a failed product".Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Drones, guns and missile shields: DAC clears Rs 2.12 lakh crore defence proposals for Armed Forces
articles.summary: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by defence minister Rajnath Singh on October 26, has accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) to capital
articles.body: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by defence minister Rajnath Singh on October 26, has accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) to capital acquisition proposals worth approximately Rs 2.12 lakh crore for the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force, with around 82 per cent of the proposed procurements expected to come from Indian industry.According to news agency ANI, the approvals cover a wide range of military equipment, including artillery systems, helicopters, counter-drone technology, surveillance and strike drones, naval missile defence systems, air defence equipment and weather radars.The DAC accorded approval for the Indian Army to procure High Mobility Vehicles, a Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System, Gun Shot Response System, Light Multi Role Helicopters, Very Short-Range Air Defence Systems, counter-drone systems, surveillance UAVs, an Integrated Surveillance and Strike System and a Long Range Kamikaze Drone System.These will strengthen mobility, firepower, battlefield surveillance and protection against aerial threats.For the Indian Navy, the DAC approved the procurement of an Active Offboard Decoy System to improve defence against modern anti-ship missiles, along with other indigenously designed and constructed naval platforms to enhance combat capabilities.For the Indian Air Force, the DAC approved the procurement of helicopters, air defence systems, weapons and Mobile X-Band Doppler Weather Radar Systems.Special Utility Helicopters will support air transport, while the radars will provide localised weather surveillance in forward areas. Light Multi Role Helicopters will serve both the Army and the Air Force.The DAC's approvals place significant emphasis on domestic defence manufacturing, with approximately 82 per cent of the proposed procurements expected to be sourced from Indian industry.

articles.title: Ghost of Yom Kippur War returns as Israel drills for surprise attack amid Iran tensions
articles.summary: Israel has launched a massive 48-hour military exercise involving multiple divisions and air force units to prepare for surprise attacks and cross-border
articles.body: Israel has launched a massive 48-hour military exercise involving multiple divisions and air force units to prepare for surprise attacks and cross-border infiltrations, amid rising tensions with Iran and renewed concerns over the possibility of a conflict similar to the 1973 Yom Kippur War.According to Fox News, the exercise focuses on strengthening Israel's readiness for attacks across multiple fronts, with military planners drawing lessons from past intelligence failures and the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack.The drills come amid heightened regional tensions, following a reported Iranian ballistic missile exercise and days before Israel's October 27 national election.The exercise involves the Israeli military's northern command's 210th division, the west bank division and the central command's 98th and 96th divisions, alongside the Israeli Air Force. The drills are designed to test the military's response to surprise attacks, cross-border infiltrations by land and air, and threats emerging across multiple fronts.IDF Chief of Staff Lt General Eyal Zamir warned that the risk of escalation had increased amid security concerns across multiple fronts.During a visit to the military's Central Command, Zamir said, "Given the numerous warnings across all fronts and the sensitivity of the current period, the potential for escalation has increased."He added that Israeli forces had reinforced deployments in several areas to strengthen operational readiness and security.The drills come days after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reportedly conducted a ballistic missile exercise, adding to concerns over a possible escalation between Tehran and Jerusalem. Israeli military preparations are also being closely watched ahead of the country's October 27 election, with security officials concerned that regional adversaries could exploit the sensitive political period.Why the 1973 Yom Kippur War still haunts IsraelThe comparison with the 1973 Yom Kippur War centres on how military exercises and troop movements can mask preparations for an actual attack.On October 6, 1973, Egypt and Syria launched a coordinated offensive against Israel on two fronts, with Egyptian forces crossing the Suez Canal and Syrian troops advancing into the Golan Heights. Israeli intelligence had received indications of unusual military activity but failed to correctly assess the likelihood and timing of the attack.Israeli national security analyst Dr Ehud Eilam told Fox News that Egypt and Syria had conducted a major exercise before the war, helping conceal their military preparations. He warned that the current confrontation carries a similar risk of miscalculation, as Israel and Iran closely monitor each other's military movements and suspect the other could strike first.In 1973, the failure to interpret warning signs correctly left Israel vulnerable in the opening phase of the war.The current drills are intended to improve readiness against surprise attacks and infiltrations, incorporating lessons from both the 1973 war and the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led assault.You use AI every day. articles.title: Delhi’s war on dust: Why city’s pollution hotspots remain a challenge
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An examination of road dust, construction violations, mechanical sweeping and whether Delhi’s civic agencies are addressing the sources of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An examination of road dust, construction violations, mechanical sweeping and whether Delhi’s civic agencies are addressing the sources of pollution or merely suppressing it after it becomes visible.Delhi’s annual battle against air pollution has brought a familiar set of interventions to its roads: water sprinklers, anti-smog guns, mechanical road sweepers and intensified cleaning drives. Yet, despite these measures, dust continues to accumulate along roads, construction material remains a concern, and civic agencies face questions over enforcement. The challenge is not simply to remove dust from the streets but to prevent it from becoming airborne in the first place.Recent reports reveal a gap between the scale of Delhi’s dust-control efforts and the persistent problems on the ground. While government agencies are expanding their equipment and targeting identified pollution hotspots, studies and inspections point to poor road conditions, inadequate mechanised cleaning, uncovered construction material and illegal dumping as continuing sources of pollution. The central question is whether the capital is moving from visible dust suppression to sustained control of the sources. The hotspots: Where does the dust come from?Delhi’s pollution hotspots are not necessarily affected by a single source. Road dust, construction activity, traffic movement, waste dumping and exposed soil can combine to worsen local air quality. Areas identified in previous hotspot assessments include Anand Vihar, Bawana, Mundka, Wazirpur, Rohini, RK Puram, Okhla, Jahangirpuri, Punjabi Bagh, Ashok Vihar and Dwarka.In October 2026, PWD introduced a strategy to identify and tackle dust sources within a 3-km radius of 47 pollution hotspots. The approach recognises that cleaning a particular road or installing dust-suppression equipment at one location may not be enough if loose soil, uncovered construction material or excavation nearby continues to release particles into the air.The identified hotspots include Anand Vihar, ITO, DTU, Dwarka, Bawana, Pusa, IGI Airport, IIT Delhi, areas near JNU, Burari Crossing, North Campus and Alipur. The department also planned to deploy around 200 anti-smog guns as part of its dust-control measures.This wider approach is significant because pollution does not stop at the boundaries of a designated hotspot. Dust generated by construction, traffic or exposed surfaces in surrounding areas can travel towards roads and neighbourhoods where suppression measures are already in place.The scale of the challenge is also reflected in the Commission for Air Quality Management's hotspot exercise. A report on September 2026 said an earlier assessment had identified 65 major pollution sources across 13 hotspots. Of these, 16 had been resolved, while 43 remained under monitoring and six were pending. Authorities had also identified 4,555 minor pollution sources, including road dust, garbage and construction-waste dumping, potholes, unpaved roads, traffic congestion and open waste burning. Nearly half of these minor problems had been addressed at the time of the review.These figures point to the scale of the task: identifying pollution sources is only the first step. The effectiveness of the strategy depends on how quickly the problems are fixed and whether the fixes last. Road sweeping: The gap between deployment and coverageMechanical road sweeping is one of the most direct ways to remove accumulated dust before passing vehicles push it back into the air. However, the coverage of these machines remains a major concern.A report published on October 23, 2026, said a CAQM assessment found that mechanical road sweepers were cleaning only 35–40% of Delhi’s large and medium-sized roads on alternate days, against the prescribed norm of covering the entire road network. Delhi had nearly 100 machines, compared with the 172 required.The assessment also found that a machine covered up to 30km a day, against a requirement of 40km. Roads obstructed by encroachments or illegally parked vehicles posed another challenge. Meanwhile, around 70% of Delhi’s road network consists of roads less than 10 metres wide, which are currently swept manually.This exposes a fundamental weakness in the city's dust-control strategy. Deploying machines is not the same as ensuring that every vulnerable stretch receives adequate cleaning. If road edges and medians continue to collect dust, or if the material lifted during sweeping is not removed, the pollution source remains.The problem was highlighted during a 2023 inspection by then Delhi lieutenant governor VK Saxena. A report said thick layers of dust and loose silt had accumulated on pavements and footpaths along stretches near the Red Fort, Rajghat, ITO, Pragati Power Plant, IP Estate and Millennium Park. Passing vehicles were stirring up the dust, while mechanical sweepers were also found blowing dust instead of suppressing it with water. Officials were directed to clean the streets and pavements and take remedial measures at power plant yards and bus depots.The implication is clear: the effectiveness of road sweeping depends not only on the number of machines but also on how they operate, whether they cover the required stretches and what happens to the dust they collect. Construction sites and waste: Enforcement remains the testConstruction and demolition activity presents another challenge because exposed soil, uncovered materials and improperly stored waste can release dust into surrounding areas.A report on March 2026 said the Prime Minister’s Office had flagged serious lapses in Delhi’s dust-mitigation measures and warned of strict action against officials for negligence. Discussions among officials covered road dust, poor waste management and delays in grievance redressal.The Municipal Corporation of Delhi said it was removing construction and demolition waste from roadsides and vacant plots on a war footing. However, district authorities cited limited mechanised sweeping in residential areas, shortages of capsules at fixed compactor transfer stations and difficulties in deploying heavy machinery in narrow lanes.The difficulties are not new. During a November 2025 meeting, MCD councillors flagged unauthorised construction despite restrictions under Graded Response Action Plan Stage III, illegal dumping of construction waste and the burning of leaves. They also alleged that water sprinkling and mechanical sweepers were being deployed only in selected wards, leaving other areas neglected. The committee chairperson acknowledged that potholes were visible across the city and that accumulated dust was hardly being lifted after sweeping.These concerns raise questions about the consistency of enforcement. Rules requiring construction materials to be covered or dust to be suppressed cannot deliver lasting results if violations continue or inspections fail to secure compliance.In October 2026, MCD stepped up monitoring by installing 360-degree cameras at all 125 construction and demolition waste sites, with live feeds to the Delhi Pollution Control Committee. It also introduced procedures for covering or wetting dumped material, installing dust barriers and ensuring that vehicles transporting construction waste are fully covered. Joint enforcement teams were tasked with acting against dust pollution, illegal dumping and biomass burning.These measures offer a way to move beyond periodic inspections. But their value will depend on whether monitoring leads to timely action against violations and whether the same locations remain compliant after inspection teams leave.Anti-smog guns and sprinklers: Suppression is not preventionDelhi has continued to expand its use of water-based dust suppression. On October 21, 2026, reported that MCD had deployed 167 water sprinklers and 60 anti-smog guns across roads, civic facilities and high-rise buildings. It had also launched deep cleaning of identified dust-prone roads across all 12 zones.However, the presence of equipment does not automatically translate into a sustained reduction in pollution. In a report on anti-smog guns, environment activist Bhavreen Malhotra said the equipment could suppress visible coarse dust in localised construction zones, but its overall impact on Delhi’s air quality was limited because it could not tackle particulate or gaseous pollutants that rise during winter. She also said the guns should ideally operate throughout the year.The distinction matters: sprinklers and anti-smog guns can help manage airborne dust, but they cannot substitute for repairing damaged roads, removing accumulated silt, covering construction material or preventing illegal dumping.What would tackling dust at its source mean?The evidence points towards a more comprehensive approach. First, road-owning agencies need to ensure that mechanical sweepers cover the required stretches, particularly pollution-prone corridors, while improving access to narrower roads. Second, potholes, unpaved surfaces and damaged road edges need attention so that dust does not repeatedly accumulate. Third, construction and demolition rules must be enforced consistently, with waste removed rather than simply shifted elsewhere.Delhi’s proposed strategy of examining dust sources within a 3-km radius of pollution hotspots could help address the problem beyond individual roads. Meanwhile, the deployment of cameras at waste sites could improve accountability if violations are detected and acted upon promptly.The city also needs to assess outcomes rather than relying only on the number of sprinklers, anti-smog guns or sweeping machines deployed. Coverage, frequency of cleaning, waste removal, repeat violations and improvements at identified hotspots are more meaningful measures of progress.Delhi’s dust problem: Why suppression measures alone can’t clear the airDelhi is expanding its dust-control operations, but reporting shows that gaps in road sweeping, poor road conditions, construction violations and waste management continue to undermine these efforts. The problem is not that water sprinkling or anti-smog guns have no role; it is that they cannot deliver lasting results on their own.The real test is whether Delhi can stop dust from accumulating and becoming airborne, rather than repeatedly suppressing it after it appears. Until road maintenance, waste removal and enforcement become consistent, the city risks continuing to chase the dust it has yet to eliminate at its source.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: New Jersey teen Joshua Haddad stopped at a crash and, with his parents, helped pull two trapped people free; the rescue has made him the first person in his state to receive the Air Force Junior ROTC Gold Valor Award
articles.summary: Heroism sometimes begins with a simple decision: to stop when others might keep moving.
articles.body: Heroism sometimes begins with a simple decision: to stop when others might keep moving. For Joshua Haddad, a New Jersey teenager returning home from church with his family, that moment came beside a wrecked vehicle on a South Jersey road. Two people were trapped inside, and Haddad, alongside his parents, stepped in to help bring them to safety. Months later, the decision has earned him one of the rarest distinctions in the Air Force Junior Reserve Officer Training Corps (AFJROTC), making him the first recipient of its Gold Valor Award in New Jersey.A roadside rescue that changed everythingAccording to Hoodline and 6 ABC Action News, the incident occurred in May 2026 near the intersection of Kings Highway and Auburn Road. Haddad, who lived in Pilesgrove, was then a cadet lieutenant colonel preparing to graduate from Salem County Vocational Technical High School.When the family came upon the crash, two occupants remained trapped inside the vehicle. Haddad and his parents rushed to help, working together to pull the victims free.The rescue would soon draw attention beyond the immediate roadside emergency. The AFJROTC Gold Valor Award was proposed for Haddad after the incident.An honour reserved for extraordinary courageThe Gold Valor Award represents the highest decoration available to an AFJROTC cadet. As reported by Hoodline and 6 ABC Action News, it is reserved for individuals who voluntarily accept life-threatening risks to save others.Salem County Vocational Technical School, as reported by Hoodline, confirmed that Haddad is the first person in New Jersey to receive the award. He is also reportedly only the sixth cadet nationwide to earn the honour over the past decade, underlining the extraordinary nature of the recognition.Unlike routine awards marking achievement or completion of the cadet programme, the Gold Valor Award requires a rigorous review. Haddad's nomination underwent a thorough investigation before receiving endorsement and final approval from AFJROTC headquarters.From cadet leadership to a lasting legacyThe recognition also highlights the broader values promoted by the Junior ROTC programme. Its objectives include developing citizenship, responsibility, self-discipline, character and community service, alongside an introduction to air and space fundamentals, according to information cited by Hoodline.Haddad's actions offered a powerful real-world example of those values, demonstrating how individual initiative and a willingness to help can make a difference in an emergency, states 6 ABC Action News report.His rescue was not presented as part of a formal emergency-response assignment. Instead, it was a spontaneous decision made in a moment of uncertainty, with his parents supporting the effort to reach the trapped occupants.A milestone for Salem TechSalem County Vocational Technical School announced that Haddad would receive the award at a formal campus ceremony on Friday, October 23, 2026, according to Hoodline. By then, he had graduated from the school where he had served as an AFJROTC cadet.For Haddad, the honour marks recognition of a single defining moment. For Salem Tech and New Jersey, it represents a historic first within the national cadet programme, claims 6 ABC Action News report.The distinction ultimately celebrates more than a rescue. It recognises the courage to act when help is needed most, and the difference one person and a family willing to step forward can make when lives are at stake.Images Courtesy: Facebook and istockYou use AI every day. articles.title: Florida python hunter captures 18-foot invasive python in Puerto Rico after it strangled a pet cat, setting a local live-capture record
articles.summary: A Florida-based python hunter has captured an 18-foot-4-inch reticulated python in Puerto Rico after the snake was reportedly spotted strangling a pet cat
articles.body: A Florida-based python hunter has captured an 18-foot-4-inch reticulated python in Puerto Rico after the snake was reportedly spotted strangling a pet cat behind a house. Kevin Pavlidis, known online as Snakeaholic, joined members of Proyecto Retic to track down the enormous reptile in Naranjito, where it had escaped into vegetation after homeowners scared it away from the animal. The team located the snake after around 20 minutes of searching and successfully captured it. Measuring approximately 5.59 metres, the python was described by local media as the longest live-captured reticulated python recorded in Puerto Rico. The incident has renewed attention on the island's invasive snake population and concerns about the threat these non-native predators pose to pets and native wildlife.Florida python hunter tracks down 18-foot python in Puerto RicoKevin Pavlidis, a Florida-based snake hunter who goes by the name Snakeaholic, responded after receiving reports of a reticulated python attacking a pet cat behind a house in Naranjito, a municipality in central Puerto Rico. According to reports, the homeowners managed to scare the snake away before it could consume the cat, and the reptile moved down a mountainside into nearby vegetation.Pavlidis worked with members of Proyecto Retic, a team involved in locating and removing invasive reticulated pythons on the island. He said it took around 20 minutes to track down the snake in the vegetation. The team eventually located it hidden in a bush, secured its head and pulled it out before completing the capture.The reticulated python measured 18 feet and four inches, or approximately 5.59 metres. Photographs shared after the capture showed several people standing shoulder-to-shoulder while holding the snake, illustrating its extraordinary length.Local newspaper El Nuevo Día reported that the capture set a record for the longest live-captured reticulated python in Puerto Rico. Reticulated pythons are among the world's longest snake species, with individuals capable of growing considerably longer than many other constrictors.Reticulated pythons are an invasive species in Puerto RicoReticulated pythons are native to South and Southeast Asia but are considered an invasive species in Puerto Rico. They are large constrictors that kill prey by wrapping around it and squeezing, and can feed on a range of animals, including mammals and birds.Their presence on the island has raised concerns about predation on native wildlife, pets and livestock. Pavlidis has said that he and Proyecto Retic are working to remove the snakes and limit their spread. However, the full size and distribution of the wild population remain uncertain, and the island's situation should not automatically be equated with Florida's better-known Burmese python problem.What happened to the python after its capture?Reports said the snake was euthanised following its capture. Pavlidis has explained that restrictions on reticulated pythons in Puerto Rico limit the options for keeping or relocating them. Removing invasive snakes is intended to prevent them from continuing to reproduce and preying on native animals.The incident also drew attention to the risk these large reptiles can pose around homes, particularly in rural areas where pets and livestock may be vulnerable.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1985, more than 40 music stars recorded “We Are the World”; proceeds from the charity single helped raise over $100 million for humanitarian work
articles.summary: In 1985, more than 40 music stars came together to record “We Are the World”, a charity single written by Lionel Richie and Michael Jackson and produced
articles.body: In 1985, more than 40 music stars came together to record “We Are the World”, a charity single written by Lionel Richie and Michael Jackson and produced by Quincy Jones to raise funds and awareness for famine relief in Ethiopia. Recorded on 28 January, the song sold more than seven million copies and raised over $80 million for humanitarian efforts across Africa. The organisation has raised more than $100 million through its wider fundraising efforts over four decades, supporting initiatives addressing poverty, hunger and long-term development in Africa, as well as hunger and homelessness in the United States.How did “We Are the World” support humanitarian efforts across AfricaAccording to USA for Africa’s, the original recording of We Are the World sold more than seven million copies and raised over $80 million to support humanitarian efforts across Africa. The organisation states that the proceeds supported work addressing both immediate humanitarian needs and longer-term challenges. The fundraising was initially connected to the famine and refugee crisis, with assistance channelled primarily through United Nations agencies and international non-governmental organisations experienced in emergency relief.USA for Africa’s account explains that its support subsequently extended beyond immediate emergency assistance. During the following two years, the organisation partnered with the US non-governmental organisation consortium InterAction to support initiatives increasingly focused on recovery and development. From late 1987, a further phase placed greater emphasis on long-term development and strengthening local capacity, including support for African non-governmental organisations and local associations representing farmers, women and young people.How did USA for Africa expand its impact beyond “We Are the World”Although the original recording raised more than $80 million, USA for Africa reports that its wider fundraising efforts over four decades have generated more than $100 million. The organisation attributes its broader legacy to both We Are the World and the Hands Across America event, which took place in 1986. Its work has supported efforts to address poverty and promote long-term sustainable development in Africa, as well as hunger and homelessness in the United States.In its account of the organisation’s history, USA for Africa explains that its funding has evolved, with support increasingly directed towards African organisations, community associations and initiatives designed to strengthen local participation. The organisation says its work has contributed to the development of African civil society organisations. It continues to support community-driven initiatives in Africa and the United States, although funding is now provided on a more modest scale than during its earlier years.How was “We Are the World” re-released for its 40th anniversaryTo mark the 40th anniversary of We Are the World, USA for Africa announced the song’s re-release in newly remastered formats. According to the organisation, the release introduced the recording in Spatial Audio and high-resolution audio formats. The anniversary initiative also made the song and an enhanced music video available to audiences, renewing access to a recording originally created to raise funds and awareness for famine relief.USA for Africa continues to describe the project as part of its broader mission to demonstrate the importance of individual participation and collective action in addressing global challenges. Its official history notes that, despite progress, hunger, conflict and other development challenges remain. The organisation’s continuing work focuses on supporting community-led initiatives and creating opportunities for lasting change. The original recording remains central to its history, having brought together more than 40 artists in 1985 and generated more than $80 million for humanitarian efforts across Africa, while the organisation’s wider fundraising has exceeded $100 million.You use AI every day.
