articles.title: A 17-year-old Missouri girl was killed while driving to a Halloween party; days later, prosecutors linked the suspect to another highway shooting and said a rifle and ammunition were recovered from his hotel room
articles.summary: A drive that should have ended with Halloween festivities instead became the beginning of a homicide investigation spanning multiple states.
articles.body: A drive that should have ended with Halloween festivities instead became the beginning of a homicide investigation spanning multiple states. Seventeen-year-old Alyssa Wilson was on her way to a Halloween event in Missouri when a bullet struck her car on a highway, killing her and cutting short a future filled with plans. Within days, investigators arrested a Texas man accused of the shooting and uncovered evidence that could connect him to another highway shooting reported earlier that month.A Halloween journey turns fatalAccording to a report by The Guardian, on October 14, Wilson was driving her Buick Encore along Interstate 170 near Overland, Missouri, on her way to Boo at the Zoo, a Halloween event at the St Louis Zoo.The Fox2Now report adds that prosecutors allege a single shot was fired into the rear of her vehicle, striking Wilson in the back and leaving her unable to control the car. The vehicle subsequently crashed into a concrete highway median. She was taken to Barnes-Jewish Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.The suspected shooter, 43-year-old Willie James Herndon of Arlington, Texas, reportedly had no known relationship with Wilson, adds The Guardian report.Herndon faces first-degree murder and armed criminal action charges in St Louis County. His wife, Taiya Herndon, 45, has also been charged with hindering prosecution, according to Fox2Now.Investigators examine an earlier shootingThe investigation took a wider turn when authorities revisited a separate shooting reported on October 11 along Interstate 55 near Bates Avenue in St Louis.According to Fox2Now, a 37-year-old motorist told police that a white SUV had pulled over near the highway shortly after 4:30 a.m. When the driver went around the vehicle, a bullet struck the rear of the motorist's car. Nobody was injured.A shell casing was recovered at the scene. Investigators are conducting laboratory and ballistic examinations to establish whether the weapon used in that incident was the same rifle allegedly used in Wilson's killing, The Guardian and Fox2Now reported.Surveillance footage and vehicle-tracking evidence have helped investigators trace a white SUV believed to be associated with Herndon across the two incidents and subsequent locations, adds the online report.Hotel arrest yields weapons and notesThe search for the suspects led authorities to a Days Inn in Caseyville, Illinois, on October 16. According to The Guardian, investigators approached Taiya Herndon outside the hotel room before Willie Herndon emerged and attempted to flee. He was subsequently arrested.A search of the room reportedly uncovered a rifle in plain view, ammunition matching the type associated with Wilson's shooting, two licence plates and handwritten notes detailing police vehicles and other vehicles Herndon allegedly believed were following him. Investigators also found a petrol station receipt linked to an area near the scene of Wilson's death.Federal prosecutors in Illinois have charged Willie Herndon with being a felon in possession of a firearm, The Guardian reported. His prior convictions include nonviolent felony offences in California, according to Fox2Now.A wider investigation into highway shootingsAuthorities are examining whether the two incidents could be connected to other unsolved cases involving apparently random attacks on motorists. Fox2Now reported that investigators have drawn comparisons with the 2024 interstate shooting death of Collin Brown, another case involving a victim with no known connection to the suspected shooter.Investigators are also reviewing the couple's movements across Texas, Arkansas and Missouri using licence plate reader data. Establishing a connection between the shootings could help law enforcement agencies identify similar cases elsewhere.The investigation has moved quickly despite the apparent randomness of Wilson's killing, with Fox2Now reporting that the Major Case Squad played a significant role in solving the homicide.For Wilson's family, however, the investigation cannot undo the loss of a teenager who had been looking forward to turning 18 and taking her first family vacation to Disney. articles.title: Broke locks, scaled walls: Congress MPs named in Jamia FIR amid students' unrest
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Breaking a university gate lock, scaling a boundary wall and allegedly damaging campus property.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Breaking a university gate lock, scaling a boundary wall and allegedly damaging campus property. These are among the incidents cited in an FIR against the Congress MPs following the students' protest at Jamia Millia Islamia.The complaint, filed by registrar Md Mahtab Alam Rizvi, alleges that Congress MPs Imran Pratapgarhi and Imran Masood entered the campus without authorisation on separate occasions as the agitation for the restoration of the students' union intensified.The FIR, registered at Jamia Nagar police station on Sunday, details a series of incidents between October 21 and 24. Pratapgarhi allegedly broke the lock of gate number 4A to enter the campus on October 21. Two days later, Masood allegedly climbed a boundary wall near Gafoor Nagar with the help of a ladder to gain entry.The complaint also flags an incident on October 24, when outsiders allegedly occupied and locked the department of political science building, disrupting academic activities. It further alleges that people who were neither students nor university employees entered the campus, defaced walls with objectionable graffiti, damaged property and manhandled university employees, leaving some injured.The allegations extend beyond the two Congress MPs.The registrar's complaint mentions Samajwadi Party MP Mohibbullah Nadvi, who was detained while on his way to the campus, as well as other political leaders who allegedly visited the protest site without prior intimation to the university administration.The FIR invokes provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to criminal trespass, wrongful restraint, voluntarily causing hurt, mischief, criminal intimidation, criminal conspiracy and common intention.It also cites the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, 1984, and the Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Property Act, 2007.The campus has been witnessing protests since October 12, with students demanding the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students' Union (JMISU), whose elections have not been held since 2006. Protesters are also seeking the withdrawal of disciplinary action against students involved in the agitation.As tensions mounted, the university moved classes across all courses online, citing concerns over students' safety and security. It has maintained that Gate No. 18 is the designated location for protests and described the gathering at the Gulistan-e-Ghalib lawns as an unauthorised occupation.The Students' Federation of India (SFI), Jamia unit, has, meanwhile, alleged that police detained students outside Gate No. 7 and that university officials tried to forcibly remove protesters, dismantle their tents and drag women students during a confrontation. articles.title: 'Beyond making weapons', Rajnath wants India to become a next-gen military tech powerhouse
articles.summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Monday said India’s push for self-reliance in defence was entering its second phase, with the focus shifting to
articles.body: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Monday said India’s push for self-reliance in defence was entering its second phase, with the focus shifting to state-of-the-art technology, globally competitive equipment and capabilities that meet the operational requirements of the armed forces.According to news agency PTI, Rajnath Singh made the remarks while addressing the plenary session of the Indian Navy’s annual seminar, Swavlamban 2026, at the Manekshaw Centre in New Delhi, where he said innovators would play the role of “impact players” in the next phase.Singh said the defence sector had performed well in the first phase of the self-reliance drive and was now entering its next stage.“The sector, in its bid to achieve self-reliance, has ‘earned good marks’ in its phase one, and now it is entering its second phase,” he said.Outlining the priorities for the next phase, Singh said the focus should be on delivering advanced capabilities while ensuring cost-effectiveness, quality and global competitiveness.In this next phase of ‘atmanirbharta’ in defence, focus should be on delivering outcomes which are of ‘top end’ and of the ‘state-of-the-art’ level,” he said.“Efforts in the second phase should also aim to achieve cost-effectiveness, global competitiveness, high quality, and output which meet the operational requirements in a larger way,” he added.Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan called for faster conversion of innovation into operational capabilities, highlighting the potential of artificial intelligence and autonomous systems to strengthen naval power.Vice chief of Naval Staff Vice Admiral Ajay Kochhar urged stakeholders to shorten the “innovation to integration” cycle.Citing the Ukraine conflict, he said rapid advances in AI, autonomous systems and cyber capabilities were reshaping warfare and could make technological advantages short-lived.

articles.title: Indian-American Texas student says he's 'politically homeless' after facing backlash for voting for Democrat: 'My biggest concern is....'
articles.summary: 21-year-old Vasant Bhatt announced on social media that despite identifying with conservative politics so far, he voted for Democrat James Talarico in the
articles.body: 21-year-old Vasant Bhatt announced on social media that despite identifying with conservative politics so far, he voted for Democrat James Talarico in the Texas election against Republican candidate Ken Paxton to reject anti-India hatred in his state and in the US. Though he is a second-generation Indian-American, he was asked to leave the US after his post went viral. The Political Science student of the University of Houston was removed from Campus Reform's correspondent program as an apparent fallout but he said he won't retract his beliefs and neither would he abandon his community.MAGA had a problem with Bhatt putting Indian first in his hyphenated Indian-American identity and still considering Indian-American as his community.In an interview with the Houston Chronicle, he said the social media reactions to his post were disturbing but not shocking. He interned for Republican senator Ted Cruz's 2024 campaign but now he considers himself as "politically homeless", but his future votes would probably go to the Democrats.“My biggest concern is the extent to which politics has become organized around just resentment,” said Bhatt told Houston Chronicle's Adrian Ashford.Rising India hatred driving Indian-Americans to DemocratsThe original post that Bhatt made was a request to every Indian-American with voting rights to go out and reject the anti-India hatred. "As a second-generation Indian American, I am thoroughly disgusted by the xenophobia, racial resentment, and increasingly brazen attacks on my identity. My family has contributed to the American story through hard work, sacrifice, and an unwavering belief in the opportunities this nation promises. I am every bit as American as anyone else, and I will not tolerate being treated as a perpetual foreigner in the country I call home," Bhatt wrote."I implore every eligible Texan to get out and vote. This election is about the kind of state and country we are prepared to defend—and the principles we refuse to surrender."Indian Americans historically favored Democrats, but the community sided with Trump in 2024. HuffPost reported that a recent poll commissioned by an Indian American advocacy group found a quarter of Indian Americans who backed Trump in 2024 planned to vote for Democrats in the midterm elections. The poll revealed that the rising cost of living and healthcare were top issues for the community, like other voters. While Democrats led Republicans among likely voters at around 66%, nearly two-thirds of Independent South Asian voters said they were undecided ahead of the midterms, the report said. “There are a large chunk of [Indian American] voters who are, for lack of a better word, having buyers remorse,” Chintan Patel, the executive director of Indian American Impact, the company that conducted the survey, told HuffPost. “That’s something that is building across the community as we’re talking about hate and discrimination.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Massachusetts gun owners face an October 28 registration deadline, six days before voters decide whether to repeal the law behind it, while Idaho voters will choose an official state gun from six historic firearms
articles.summary: As voters get ready to cast their ballots in the upcoming U.S. elections, gun laws and firearm history have become important topics on state ballots.
articles.body: As voters get ready to cast their ballots in the upcoming U.S. elections, gun laws and firearm history have become important topics on state ballots. In Massachusetts, gun owners are rushing to meet an October 28 registration deadline. The deadline comes just six days before voters decide whether to repeal the law that created it. Meanwhile, in Idaho, voters are making a symbolic choice of their own. They are choosing an official state firearm from a list of six historic weapons. These different measures show how states across the United States are taking different approaches to gun ownership, regulation and local culture ahead of Election Day on November 3.Registration requirement in MassachusettsThe upcoming deadline in Massachusetts comes from House Bill 4885, also known as Chapter 135. Governor Maura Healey signed the wide-ranging gun law into effect. According to reporting by the Associated Press, the law created a required electronic system to track firearm ownership across the state. Under the law, gun owners must register all firearms that have not been recorded before. This includes grandfathered assault-style rifles. Owners must register these weapons through the state's online portal by October 28. The law also introduces strict new rules for serial numbers on firearm frames and receivers. It places limits on ghost guns and strengthens safety training requirements for people applying for firearm licences. Supporters say the online system gives law enforcement important tools to fight illegal gun trafficking and track weapons that cannot be traced. The Associated Press reported that public safety advocates see the registration system as a necessary step towards improving state oversight and preventing violent crime.Opponents push for referendum repealGun owners and civil rights groups in Massachusetts have strongly opposed the October 28 registration deadline. Opponents, led by the Civil Rights Coalition, collected enough signatures to put Question 9 on the November 3 ballot. A veto referendum allows voters to decide whether to keep or repeal House Bill 4885 in full. Under state referendum rules, voting "no" would repeal the law, while voting "yes" would keep it in place. According to legal updates from the Serpa Law Office, the timing of the vote has caused considerable confusion among gun owners across the state. Since the registration deadline comes six days before Election Day, gun owners are still legally required to register their firearms. Failing to register by October 28 is a criminal offence under current state law. Even if voters repeal the law on November 3, that decision will not erase violations committed while the law was in effect. Opponents say the short time available for registration places an unfair burden on law-abiding citizens. They also argue that the law defines prohibited firearm features too broadly. In their view, this could turn people who previously owned legal firearms into offenders without giving them clear guidance about the rules.Idaho voters to choose official firearmWhile Massachusetts debates stricter gun oversight, voters in Idaho are considering a non-binding referendum to choose an official state firearm. The ballot measure began with House Bill 932, which passed both chambers of the Idaho Legislature with unanimous support before Governor Brad Little signed it into law. According to reporting by the Associated Press and local news outlet KTVB, the advisory question asks voters to choose one of six historic firearms. The goal is to recognise Idaho's frontier history and contributions to the military.The options listed on the Idaho ballot include:Winchester Model 1894 (.30-30)Winchester Model 1873 "Gun that Won the West" (.44-40)1873 Colt Single Action Army Revolver "Peacemaker" (.45 Colt)M1 Garand rifle (.30-06)Colt M1911 .45 automatic Colt pistol (.45 ACP)Remington Model 700 bolt-action rifle (.30-06)Symbolic choice versus legislative actionUnlike the Massachusetts registration requirement, the vote in Idaho will not immediately change state law. According to Ballotpedia and KREM-TV, the measure is an advisory vote intended to help guide lawmakers in future legislative sessions. The firearm that receives the most votes will not automatically become Idaho's official state gun. State lawmakers will still need to prepare and pass formal legislation in a later session to make the designation official. Supporters of the measure include state Representative Jason Monks, who sponsored the bill. They argue that choosing an official state firearm would honour Idaho's long history of hunting, sport shooting and firearm manufacturing. However, the proposal has received some criticism from commentators who question whether an advisory vote needs to appear on an already lengthy election ballot. The Idaho Statesman noted that while many people support recognising the state's heritage, some civic observers believe the choice could have been made through an online survey instead of an official ballot question. Both state measures show how guns remain an important issue for voters. In Massachusetts, the debate centres on meeting new legal requirements, while in Idaho, the focus is on recognising the state's history and culture.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: Samuel Sey, a Ghana-born conservative Christian blogger who has publicly defended US President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown and mass deportation
articles.body: Samuel Sey, a Ghana-born conservative Christian blogger who has publicly defended US President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown and mass deportation policies, has been detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and is facing removal from the United States. The 39-year-old was detained at Columbus International Airport in Ohio on October 21 and is being held at Butler County Jail, according to reports. His detention has drawn attention because of his outspoken support for strict immigration enforcement.The Department of Homeland Security told Religion News Service that Sey entered the United States legally in 2022 but overstayed his authorized period of admission by more than four years. The department also said he had no pending immigration applications and had accepted voluntary departure.“He will remain in ICE custody until removed from the United States,” a DHS spokesperson told Religion News Service.Sey’s supporters, however, have suggested that his detention could be linked to an administrative or paperwork issue. Conservative Christian commentators have rallied behind him, with some disputing the circumstances surrounding his arrest.A fundraising appeal set up for Sey’s family said his wife, Annie, was seeking his release on bail to resolve possible clerical issues concerning his immigration status. The couple has three children.Who is Samuel Sey?Sey was born in Ghana and moved to Canada as a child before relocating to the United States in 2022. He is a Christian writer, blogger, schoolteacher and political commentator whose work focuses on religion, race, culture and politics.He runs the website Slow to Write and has contributed to conservative and Christian publications. He has also participated in podcasts and public discussions on religious and political issues.Sey has spoken publicly about his childhood in Ghana, including the financial difficulties his family faced and his separation from his mother, who moved to Canada in search of better opportunities. He later reunited with her there.Sey’s support for Trump’s immigration crackdownSey has repeatedly defended stricter immigration enforcement and argued that deportations are compatible with Christian teachings.“Christian ethics do not denounce deportations. articles.title: Two California artists turned around 5,000 pounds of discarded plastic into an 82-foot blue whale in 2018; after moving to New Mexico, the record-setting sculpture was named a Roadside America Sight of the Week in 2026
articles.summary: Standing 82 feet long on the high-desert campus of Santa Fe Community College in New Mexico, a life-sized blue whale made entirely from discarded trash
articles.body: Standing 82 feet long on the high-desert campus of Santa Fe Community College in New Mexico, a life-sized blue whale made entirely from discarded trash continues to attract attention from around the world. Its huge size and message about protecting the environment have made it a notable attraction. Created in 2018 by California-based artists Joel Dean Stockdill and Yustina Salnikova, the sculpture is named "Ethyl the Whale". It was built using about 5,000 pounds of single-use plastic waste. After being moved from California to its permanent home in New Mexico, the record-setting artwork was named a Roadside America Sight of the Week in 2026, bringing further attention to its importance as a cultural attraction. The giant artwork highlights the growing problem of ocean pollution. It also shows how everyday waste can be turned into public art.Turning plastic waste into life-sized artThe project began when the Monterey Bay Aquarium asked Stockdill and Salnikova to create a striking artwork showing the problem of marine pollution. To show the amount of plastic waste entering natural environments, the artists designed the sculpture to match the exact size of a fully grown blue whale. According to Guinness World Records, the completed artwork set the official record for the largest recycled plastic sculpture. Building the sculpture required a huge recycling effort. The artists collected thousands of pounds of used plastic waste, including trash bags, milk jugs and plastic containers. Working in San Francisco, they melted the discarded plastic and reshaped it into strong panels. These panels formed the outer body of the giant sea creature. "We really wanted to embrace that issue, while showing that there is a way, that it's not just despair," Stockdill said in an interview with New Mexico Magazine, explaining the purpose of the project. "There are solutions within this problem." Choosing a blue whale was an important part of the message. According to information published by the Monterey Bay Aquarium when the sculpture was first unveiled, the weight of the plastic used to make Ethyl represented the amount of plastic waste entering the world's oceans every nine minutes at the time.Relocation to New MexicoAfter its first display in the San Francisco Bay Area, the sculpture needed a permanent home with enough space for an 82-foot installation. The arts collective Meow Wolf bought Ethyl and donated the giant sculpture to Santa Fe Community College in 2019. Moving the sculpture across state lines required careful planning and presented several challenges. The artwork was taken apart, transported across the American Southwest and then carefully put back together on the college grounds. According to Santa Fe Community College, Ethyl was placed in a prominent spot on campus. It serves as both an outdoor learning exhibit and a local landmark. The college included the sculpture in its sustainability education programme, encouraging students and visitors to think about the long-term effects of single-use packaging.National recognition as a roadside landmarkSince arriving in New Mexico, the recycled whale has become a popular stop for travelers, school groups and art lovers passing through the Southwest. The landmark gained further recognition when Roadside America, a publication that features unusual travel destinations across the United States, named Ethyl the Whale a Sight of the Week. The recognition brought renewed national attention to the sculpture's design and its message about protecting the environment. The sculpture's outer surface, made from recycled polyethylene, has held up against the high elevation and changing seasonal weather in the Santa Fe area. College officials note that its location in the high desert creates a striking contrast. A creature from the deep ocean stands in a dry landscape, reminding visitors that plastic pollution affects ecosystems around the world, no matter where they are.Ongoing impact of the installationSchools and environmental groups continue to point to Ethyl as an example of how art can support sustainability. The sculpture remains open to the public on the Santa Fe Community College campus, where visitors can walk alongside the entire 82-foot structure. By turning discarded plastic into a public monument that teaches people about pollution, Stockdill and Salnikova created a lasting landmark. Their work combines artistic skill with a clear message about protecting the environment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Vivek Ramaswamy is bad publicity: Ohio venues cancel campaign events amid backlash over ad featuring Amy Acton's mother; people leave one-star review on Google
articles.summary: Several venues in Ohio have withdrawn from hosting campaign events featuring Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy as backlash intensifies
articles.body: Several venues in Ohio have withdrawn from hosting campaign events featuring Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy as backlash intensifies over an advertisement targeting his Democratic rival, Amy Acton, and featuring her estranged mother. The cancellations come days before the November 3 midterm elections, as Ramaswamy faces criticism from Democrats and fellow Republicans over the campaign advertisement.The Old Dog Ale House & Brewery in Delaware, Ohio, cancelled a Republican campaign event featuring Ramaswamy on Friday, according to USA Today reporter Jessie Balmert. The Ohio Republican Party said it had selected a new location for the event.Other businesses and event hosts have also reconsidered hosting Ramaswamy's campaign tour at their venues as people are leaving one-star reviews for these sites on Google“We’re getting calls that people don’t want him there,” a top Ohio Republican told Zeteo, a news website founded by Mehdi Hasan. The report claimed that some business owners explicitly said that they don't want public anger.Elliot's Wood Fired Kitchen in Newark said in the comments section of a recent Facebook post that it would not host the Ohio GOP's planned event on Tuesday, Newsweek reported. The Ohio Republican Party's bus tour website now lists the location of the event as "to be announced."Venues that already hosted GOP events over the weekend have received a wave of one-star Google reviews, including Kick-N-Ax in Zanesville, Izzy's in Monroe, and The Local Bar Strongsville. Some reviewers included photos of Ramaswamy at the venues.Vivek Ramaswamy says his mother was also defamedThe controversy centres on a 60-second advertisement produced by Ramaswamy's campaign that features Acton's estranged mother, Donna Arthur, accusing her daughter of lying about her childhood and personal history.“I love my daughter, but when I saw her lying about her opponent—and it's not easy for a mother to say this—but Amy has a serious problem,” Arthur said in the advertisement. “She is a liar. She lies about her past. She says she grew up living in a tent. None of that is true. She's lied her entire life,” she saidActon, a former director of the Ohio Department of Health, has spoken publicly about experiencing childhood abuse and homelessness. Her brother, Philip Stearns, has defended her account of their childhood and criticized Ramaswamy for using the family's history in a political advertisement.Arthur lost custody of her children decades ago after her husband, Cledith Arthur, was charged with sexually abusing Acton when she was a child. He pleaded not guilty, was indicted by a grand jury and subsequently failed to appear in court. He later died.Acton has said she has not spoken to her mother since she was 12 years old.The advertisement has prompted criticism from prominent Republicans, including Ohio Governor Mike DeWine, who urged Ramaswamy's campaign to stop airing it. “It's wrong to run this ad,” DeWine said, describing it as “deeply, deeply troubling”.Ramaswamy said he did not start the fight, but he is finishing it after he found himself in this fight. articles.summary: K R Jayan, known as ‘Plavu’ Jayan, wins the PV Thampy Memorial Endowment Award for planting and nurturing nearly 1 lakh jackfruit trees in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
articles.body: Kochi: K R Jayan, fondly called ‘Plavu‘ Jayan, has been selected for this year’s PV Thampy Memorial Endowment award for environment protection, instituted in memory of journalist and environmentalist P V Thampy.Jayan, 61, of Avittathoor in Irinjalakuda, is most known for his role in planting and nurturing nearly one lakh jackfruit trees across Keralam and Tamil Nadu in the past 27 years, earning him the moniker ‘Plavu Jayan‘.Growing up among trees, climbing them and forming an instinctive bond with nature shaped his sense of responsibility towards its protection. His early affinity towards jackfruit developed into a mission and a lasting commitment to the conservation of indigenous jackfruit species in Keralam.He developed nine ‘plavu‘ villages where he cultivated jackfruit trees on arid land without removing other indigenous tree species to ensure the biodiversity.For Jayan, his responsibility was not merely germinating a jackfruit seed and plant the sapling. Instead, he selected the indigenous one, isolated the seed which can retain the quality of the mother tree, raised saplings and planted it. Under his supervision, the sapling would be nurtured until they grew to nearly six feet.“I started by planting the saplings on roadsides in my neighbourhood and used to observe its growth. Later I extended to other parts along with studying the indigenous ones. Though all seeds in the jackfruits may germinate and grow, all seeds won’t have the quality of mother tree. Hence, using traditional knowledge, I isolate the seeds which can retain the quality of mother tree and raise saplings. There are around 24 indigenous jackfruit species in the state,” said Jayan.He recently sent Rs 16,000 to a landowner in Malappuram to buy authentic Thenvarikka jackfruits once they ripen.The award function will be held on Saturday with chief minister V D Satheesan presenting the award.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kochi | Silver Rate in Kochi | Bank Holidays in Kochi | Public Holidays in KochiStay updated with the latest Kochi news. articles.summary: LUCKNOW: The UP BJP on Monday announced its 712-member state working committee, barely four days ahead of a meeting to lay out the broad contours of its
articles.body: LUCKNOW: The UP BJP on Monday announced its 712-member state working committee, barely four days ahead of a meeting to lay out the broad contours of its poll strategy for the high-stakes UP assembly elections due early next year.The meeting is expected to be attended by BJP chief poll strategist and Union home minister Amit Shah, besides several other senior leaders, including national general secretary and UP in-charge Vinod Tawde and chief minister Yogi Adityanath.The committee comprises 548 regular members, 30 permanent invitees and 134 special invitees. The new committee has 267 more members than the previous one, announced in 2021 during the tenure of Swatantra Dev Singh, which had 445 members.The list, released by state BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary, includes party functionaries and leaders from across the state’s six organisational regions — West, Braj, Kanpur, Awadh, Kashi and Gorakhpur.The Gorakhpur region, Adityanath’s political backyard, has the highest representation in the state executive, with 120 members. It is followed by the Kashi region, which includes Varanasi, the constituency of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with 108 members. The Awadh region, which includes Lucknow and Ayodhya, has 104 members, followed by Kanpur with 79, West with 70 and Braj with 67.The 30 permanent invitees include Prime Minister Narendra Modi, defence minister Rajnath Singh, senior BJP leader Murli Manohar Joshi, chief minister Yogi Adityanath and the two deputy chief ministers, Keshav Maurya and Brajesh Pathak. UP ministers, including Surya Pratap Shahi and Bhupendra Chaudhary, have also been included in the list of permanent invitees. Union ministers Hardeep Puri, BL Verma, Jitin Prasad, SP Singh Baghel, Kamlesh Paswan and Kiri Vardhan Singh are also among them.Three Muslim leaders — former cabinet minister Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi, BJP Minority Morcha national president Basit Ali and BJP MLC Tariq Mansoor — have also been included in the list of permanent invitees.The list of special invitees comprises 134 members, including former national general secretaries Arun Singh and Dr RMD Agarwal. Several UP ministers, including Suresh Khanna, Baby Rani Maurya, Laxmi Narayan Chaudhary, Jaiveer Singh, Yogendra Upadhyay, Nand Gopal Nandi, Vijay Rajbhar and Dara Singh Chauhan, have also been included.Former Samajwadi Party MLA Manoj Pandey, who was recently inducted into the Yogi cabinet, has also been included as a special invitee. Pandey remains an “unattached member” of the UP assembly and is yet to formally join the BJP.The increase in the numerical strength of the new state working committee is seen as a move to accommodate the growing pool of party functionaries who were left out of the recent organisational restructuring.Discontent among party workers who were not accommodated in the organisational set-up or given other positions has been simmering within the state leadership for several days.The formation of the state working committee is seen as a key step towards putting the party’s organisational machinery in place ahead of the meeting. The body is expected to play an important role in translating the leadership’s electoral priorities into ground-level action through the party’s regional and district units.The timing of the announcement is significant, coming amid efforts by the BJP’s state leadership to consolidate its organisation and strengthen its election preparedness against an assertive Opposition, primarily the Samajwadi Party and its ally, the Congress.Sources said the October 30 meeting is expected to focus on the party’s broader electoral blueprint, organisational preparedness and coordination among its state, regional and district-level leadership. articles.title: Pay-off case: Kerala HC puts vigilance probe against Pinarayi Vijayan and others on hold
articles.summary: Kerala HC stays vigilance probe in CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case against ex-CM Pinarayi Vijayan, relatives; appeals admitted, final hearing on Nov 25.
articles.body: Kochi: The high court on Monday directed the vigilance to keep the investigation against former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and his relatives in the CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case in abeyance until further orders and stayed the single bench order directing the registration of vigilance cases.A bench of Justices K Natarajan and Johnson John was considering appeals by Vijayan and others after Supreme Court set aside an earlier division bench order and restored the appeals for fresh consideration. The court admitted the appeals and posted them for final hearing on Nov 25.Senior counsel for the appellants, including Sidharth Luthra and N Hariharan, challenged the registration of the cases, arguing that the appellants were entitled to be heard before an investigation was initiated. They relied on Section 175(4) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act (PC Act), which provides for prior approval before an inquiry or inquiry into certain allegations against public servants. They also cited provisions of the Companies Act concerning the sharing of information between investigative agencies. They further contended that an SFIO investigation into the same transaction had been stayed by Delhi HC. Referring to Section 212(2) of the Companies Act, they also argued that no other agency could investigate the matter while SFIO was conducting a probe.Advocate general K Jaju Babu submitted that the state govt had constituted a team to conduct a preliminary inquiry after receiving information from Enforcement Directorate (ED). However, the single bench intervened within two days and directed the registration of vigilance cases, following which two FIRs were registered.Additional solicitor general P Sreekumar, appearing for ED, argued that there was nothing wrong with registering cases under the PC Act based on ED’s recommendation. He also submitted that ED had registered an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) and initiated an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) following the registration of the vigilance cases.The case originated from a communication sent by ED to the state police chief recommending the registration of a case under the PC Act against Vijayan, his daughter T Veena, son-in-law P A Mohamed Riyas, a former minister, and others in connection with the alleged pay-off. HC had directed a special investigation team (SIT) to conduct a preliminary inquiry into ED’s recommendation before registering an FIR. However, acting on a petition filed by political activist K M Shajahan challenging this procedure, the single bench set aside the arrangement and directed the registration of a case under the PC Act.Vijayan and others subsequently filed leave applications seeking permission to challenge the order, contending that it had been passed without hearing them. The division bench dismissed the applications and appeals, holding that an accused public servant had no right to be heard before an FIR was registered. The appellants then approached Supreme Court through special leave petitions. articles.title: ‘Freedom from Freedom Park’: Activists warn of disobedience on Nov 28 if protest curbs in Bengaluru are not revoked
articles.summary: Bengaluru civil society groups urge govt to revoke Freedom Park-only protest curbs, warn mass disobedience on Nov 28 if not withdrawn by Nov 26.
articles.body: Bengaluru: A civil society group Monday urged the govt to withdraw restrictions limiting protests to Freedom Park. It passed a resolution warning of stronger resistance if the order is not revoked by Nov 26.The decision was made at a round-table discussion convened by Campaign for the Right to Protest at Gandhi Bhavan. The participants reiterated that the 2021 police order restricting protests must be revoked immediately.“If the city can be divided into five zones and the police commissionerates be broken into smaller divisions for administrative convenience, why shouldn’t there be more places to protest? Why should everyone, irrespective of whether they are staying in Electronics City or near Devanahalli, travel several kilometres through traffic to reach Freedom Park to protest?” the group said.The participants included members of trade unions and representatives of dalit, women, civil liberty, environment, student and LGBTQ+ groups.Historian Ramachandra Guha termed the stance of the Congress govt in the state as hypocritical. “In any city of a democratic country, protests take place at a place visible to the public. Bengaluru too must demand that... The hypocrisy of the Congress govt needs to be called out,” Guha stated.The right to protest must be reclaimed to save the Constitution and defend the foundation of democracy, the participants said and urged the govt to put an end to its “double standard” on the matter.S Babu, a street vendor of Karnataka Pragathipara Beedi Vyaparigala Sangha, said it is difficult for workers who are denied basic protections guaranteed by the Constitution to hold protests because of the restrictions.Sujatha, representing Sadhana Mahila Sangha, a non-profit working for the rights, safety and health of sex workers in Karnataka, said that the restriction to Freedom Park affects sex workers too: “Usually, when our sex workers are unlawfully detained in a police station, beaten or threatened by police, our protest outside the police station helps mount pressure to ensure their release. That is why we too demand that this restriction must be revoked.”The gathering also demanded that all FIRs registered for protesting outside Freedom Park be quashed.“If the state govt fails to revoke this licensing order by then (Nov 26), we will launch a city-wide mass disobedience movement on Nov 28. Pressure will be sustained continuously until these restrictions are lifted,” activist Vinay Sreenivasa explained.They also stated that the Campaign for the Right to Protest will convene another meeting to form a formal central committee.Restrictions via HC orderOn March 3, 2022, a division bench of HC passed an interim order directing the state govt to ensure that protests, processions and similar activities were held only at Freedom Park and nowhere else in Bengaluru.The court also directed that such activities be organised without adversely affecting traffic, particularly during rush hours, and that action be taken wherever traffic was disrupted.
